Plot the estimated dependence network

Source: R/interpret.R
mc_plot_network.Rd

Draws the response variables as nodes on a circular layout. GGM edges are weighted by partial correlations; DAG arrows are weighted by the structural coefficients \(\gamma\) of the ordered modified Cholesky factorization, and each arrow stops at the border of the node it points to. Edge width encodes magnitude, saturating at an absolute weight of one, and color encodes sign (blue positive, red negative). The graphical parameters are restored on exit.

Usage

mc_plot_network(fit, threshold = 0.05, edge_labels = FALSE)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

threshold

an edge is drawn when the absolute value of its weight exceeds threshold: the partial correlation for a GGM fit, the coefficient \(\gamma\) for a DAG fit. The coefficient is on the scale of the Pearson residuals and is not bounded by one, so the same value of threshold does not select comparably in the two layers.

edge_labels

logical; if TRUE, annotate edges with the rounded weight.

Value

Invisibly, the \(R \times R\) matrix of weights (partial correlations for the GGM layer; for the DAG layer, \(\gamma\) in the position \((i, j)\) of each arrow from \(i\) to \(j\), zero elsewhere), with the response names as dimnames. The plot is drawn on the current graphics device.

See also

mc_get_graph, mc_partial_cor

Other graph interpretation: mc_get_graph(), mc_partial_cor(), mc_partial_cor_delta()

Examples

set.seed(1); n <- 200; x <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = rnorm(n), y2 = rnorm(n), y3 = rnorm(n), x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x, y2~x, y3~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_plot_network(f)
